texts.preamble: Amitha H vs Thippeswamy on 15 July, 2025 Scch-13 1 Mvc.1026/2024 Kabc020059362024 Before The Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru (Scch.13) Dated The 15th Day Of July 2024 Present: Smt.Shyla S.M., B.B.M. Ll.B., Ii Addl.Judge & Acjm, Court of Small Causes Bengaluru M.V.C.No.1026/2024 Petitioner : Mr. Amitha.H S/o.Hanumantharaju, Aged about 19 years, R/At C.N.Durga Hobli, Mallekavu, Tumkuru-572129. (By Sri.B.H.Chikkanna, Adv.,) Vs. Respondents : 1. Sri. Thippeswamy, S/o.Cholappa, R/At No.01,1st Cross, Srs Layout, Hesaraghatta Hobli, Bengaluru Scch-13 2 Mvc.1026/2024 Achitanagar, Bengalur Rural-560107. (Rc owner of Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-V-8527) (Exparte) 2. The Manager, The Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co.Ltd., No. Golden Heights, 4th Floor, Amitha H vs Thippeswamy on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65716519/ 1 No.1/2, 59th C Cross, 4th M Block, Rajajinagar, Benglauru-560010. (Policy No.OG-24-1701-1826- 00011152 Valid from 10.06.2023 to 09.06.2024) (By Sri.V.Shrihari Naidu, Adv.) Judgment
texts.facts: This petition under Section 166 MV Act is filed by the Petitioner seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident. 2. It is stated that on 13-01-2024, at about 8:30 PM, the petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing registration number KA-52-V-8527( hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) near MuthurayanSwamy Temple, on Thumbadi-Siddhara- Betta Road, Kasaba Hobli, Tumkur, within the jurisdiction of Koratagere Police Station, Tumkur District. At that time, the rider of the said offending motorcycle was riding the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, at high speed, and as a result, dashed into an electric pole. Due to the tremendous impact, the petitioner fell down, causing him to sustain grievous injuries. He was immediately shifted to the Government Hospital, Bengaluru, where he received first-aid treatment, and thereafter shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, where he underwent in- patient treatment. It is submitted that the petitioner incurred substantial medical and incidental expenses for his treatment, recovery, and related needs. 3. At the time of the accident, the petitioner was 19 years of age and pursuing his 2nd year PUC at the Government College, Peenya, 1st Stage, Bengaluru. Due to the injuries sustained in the said accident, the petitioner has been unable to continue his education, resulting in loss of academic year, mental distress, and emotional suffering. Moreover, he has been unable to attend classes or engage in any income-generating activity, resulting in loss of education and loss of prospective income. The accident was solely caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the offending vehicle. In view of the above facts and circumstances, the petitioner humbly prays that this Hon'ble Tribunal be pleased to award compensation of Rs. 15,00,000/- along with interest, from the respondents, jointly and severally, in the interest of justice and equity. 4. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.2 has appeared through counsel and filed the written statement. The Respondent No.1 has not remained absent and was accordingly placed exparte. 5. Respondent No. 2, the insurer, has admitted the issuance of an insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle and has acknowledged that the policy was in force as on the date of the accident. However, it has been contended that its liability is subject to the terms and conditions stipulated in the insurance policy. The insurer further asserted that the owner of the motorcycle bearing Amitha H vs Thippeswamy on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65716519/ 2 registration number KA-52-B- 8527 had intentionally permitted three persons to ride on the motorcycle, despite being fully aware that the seating capacity was restricted to two persons only. This is a clear violation of traffic and insurance regulations. Further stated that the complaint, FIR, charge sheet, and other police records clearly reflect that three persons were travelling on the motorcycle at the time of the accident. Moreover, it has been specifically contended that the rider of the motorcycle did not possess a valid driving licence at the relevant time, which amounts to a breach of policy conditions. It has been alleged that the injured petitioner was not wearing a helmet at the time of the accident, which constitutes a violation of statutory safety requirements and is a contributory factor to the injuries sustained. 7. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in support of his case, doctor is examined as PW-2 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.18. The Respondent No.2 got examined its Assistant Manager as RW.1 and got marked 5 documents as per Ex.R1 to Ex.R5. 8.
texts.arguments: Hence, it is contended that the respondent insurer cannot be held liable for the injuries caused to the petitioner, as the accident and resulting injuries were attributable to the negligence of the petitioner himself, in violation of traffic laws and policy terms. The petitioner was 19 years old as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 18. The notional income taken as Rs 16,500 x 12 x 18 x 9/100= Rs.3,20,760 /- towards loss of future income. 26. Loss of amenities of life: undoubtedly the petitioner is suffering from difficulties in performing day to day activities and is facing continuous hardship due to the disability. Therefore this tribunal finds to appropriate to award a sum .40,000/- under head of loss of amenities of life.
texts.respondent_arguments: Hence, it is contended that the respondent insurer cannot be held liable for the injuries caused to the petitioner, as the accident and resulting injuries were attributable to the negligence of the petitioner himself, in violation of traffic laws and policy terms. The petitioner was 19 years old as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 18. The notional income taken as Rs 16,500 x 12 x 18 x 9/100= Rs.3,20,760 /- towards loss of future income. 26. Loss of amenities of life: undoubtedly the petitioner is suffering from difficulties in performing day to day activities and is facing continuous hardship due to the disability. Therefore this tribunal finds to appropriate to award a sum .40,000/- under head of loss of amenities of life.
